why: The diff adds `+ 1` to pageCount; the consequence is that it returns one page more than the items need, and no phrasing of that appears in the diff text. Expecting the consequence rather than the `+ 1` token is deliberate: `+ 1` can be echoed straight out of the added line without understanding it, so it cannot distinguish a review that found the bug from one that quoted the hunk. The array accepts equivalent phrasings of the same finding (`extra page`, `one page too many`, …) so the case scores whether the review found it, not whether it picked one wording. `off-by-one` is deliberately NOT accepted: paired with the required `pageCount` it can be satisfied by a review that only describes the `clampPage` hunk. `increases the page count` was added after a prompt experiment made the model state the same finding that way, which the group would otherwise have scored as silence. Restating the added line ('adds 1 to the result') or judging it ('unnecessary', 'incorrect') is deliberately NOT accepted either: that prose is available from the hunk alone, and in a measured run it came from reviews that said adding 1 was unnecessary without ever saying what the bug does, which is exactly the echo this case has to separate from understanding. A review has to state the consequence in some form to pass.

The diff REPLACES `lastPage - 1` with `lastPage` — a fix — and changes nothing else: it diffs the first state against the last, where `pageCount` is identical in both, so this case sends a DIFFERENT prompt from the other two and scores an independent sample. A review that reads deleted lines as current reports `lastPage - 1` as live behaviour and fails; one that says it was removed or replaced passes. The matcher is SENTENCE-scoped: a sentence framing the value as removed, replaced, restored, previously returned, what the original code did, or negated just before it (without adding an extra page) passes, a sentence with no such framing fails, and `still`/`keeps` beats a removal word in the same sentence; a `-` line in a pasted diff counts as the removal. `expect` exists because `expect_absent` alone is satisfied by SILENCE: a review that never mentions `clampPage` passes without looking at the change. `clampPage` and `lastPage` are identifiers, not prose, so wording cannot false-fail a review that addresses it; direction is scored only by `expect_absent`.

This diff's only change is a correct fix: it removes the `+ 1` the previous commit added, so `pageCount` is right in both revisions and there is no defect anywhere in this range. A review that flags it is reporting code that is visibly correct — the false-positive twin of the phantom case. Two needles, because one was not enough in practice: a real answer wrote 'pageCount adds an extra page by … adding 1' with no `+` anywhere, so the `+ 1` needle missed exactly the false positive this case exists to catch. 'extra page' is the consequence phrasing a review only produces if it read the fix as the bug; 'the diff removes the + 1' and 'no longer adds an extra page' are attributed and pass. Caveat: a bare 'there is no extra page' with no removal word in its sentence would false-fail, so a correct review is expected to attribute the change. A recommendation to undo the fix ('Revert the change … adding `+ 1` back') does not count as attribution despite containing 'revert': an imperative that starts the sentence asserts the removed value belongs in the new code, which is the false positive this case scores.
